protocol_reference.usage_note: The initial prioritization decision is scored against ESI acuity logic: a patient with abnormal vitals and altered mental status outranks a patient with normal vitals and an isolated stable injury, regardless of who is more vocal about pain.

note: All names, vitals, and clinical details below are entirely fictional training content generated for simulation purposes.

dialogue: Doctor, two patients just arrived together from the same road traffic accident.
An 8-year-old boy, Farhan, and a 45-year-old woman, Lakshmi -- she's his aunt.
We only have you and me right now. Who would you like to assess first?

patients.name: Farhan Sheikh
patients.chief_complaint: Passenger in road traffic accident, drowsy, abdominal tenderness

medical_report.name: Farhan Sheikh
medical_report.presenting_complaint: Rear-seat passenger in low-speed collision, complaining of abdominal pain, increasingly drowsy since arrival
medical_report.triage_category_esi: ESI-2 (abnormal vitals plus altered mental status; high-risk for occult internal injury)

patients.name: Lakshmi Devi
patients.chief_complaint: Closed deformity of the left forearm, severe pain, fully alert
patients.arrival_mode: Brought in by ambulance, same accident

initial_vitals.consciousness: Alert, in visible pain, repeatedly calling out

medical_report.name: Lakshmi Devi
medical_report.presenting_complaint: Left forearm struck door frame during collision; visible deformity, unable to move wrist, pain 8/10
medical_report.triage_category_esi: ESI-4 (single stable extremity injury, normal vitals, no resource beyond X-ray and splinting expected)

nurse_dialogue: Doctor, we have two patients. Farhan is drowsy and his belly is tender. Lakshmi is in a lot of pain from her arm but talking to us clearly.
Who would you like to assess first?

options.text: Assess Farhan first -- his drowsiness and abnormal vitals suggest a higher-acuity problem.
options.protocol_alignment: ESI-correct prioritization: altered mental status + abnormal vitals outranks a stable painful injury

effect_on_P2.vitals_delta: unchanged, safe to wait -- Nurse Maya applies a temporary sling and ice

nurse_response: Good call, Doctor. I'll keep Lakshmi comfortable with a sling while you see Farhan.

options.text: Assess Lakshmi first -- she is the one clearly in distress and asking for help.
options.protocol_alignment: Prioritizes the louder complaint over objective acuity; a classic ESI-triage error
nurse_response: Doctor, while you were splinting Lakshmi's arm, Farhan has become harder to rouse.
I think we need to see him urgently now.

options.text: Try to check on both at the same time, splitting your attention.
options.protocol_alignment: No clear prioritization; slows both assessments and delays the higher-acuity patient

effect_on_P2.vitals_delta: unchanged, but pain score rises to 9/10 from delay in analgesia

nurse_response: Doctor, going back and forth is costing us time with Farhan -- his observations are slipping.

options.text: Ask Nurse Maya to decide who should be seen first.
options.protocol_alignment: Defers the clinical prioritization decision that is the doctor's responsibility
nurse_response: Doctor, I'd say Farhan needs you first -- and honestly, every second we spent deciding mattered. He's more drowsy now.

nurse_dialogue: Farhan is drowsy and his abdomen is tender, Doctor. What would you like to do?

options.text: Perform a rapid ABCDE primary survey, get IV access, and send urgent bloods plus a FAST-equivalent abdominal scan.
options.protocol_alignment: ABCDE-consistent primary survey for suspected internal bleeding in a trauma patient
nurse_response: Scan shows free fluid in the abdomen, Doctor -- likely a splenic injury. IV access secured.
What would you like to do next?

options.text: Wait and reassess him again in a few minutes.
options.protocol_alignment: Delay in a trauma patient with abnormal vitals and altered mental status
nurse_response: Doctor, he's becoming much harder to rouse and his pressure is dropping fast.

options.text: Take a full history from the accompanying family before examining him.
options.protocol_alignment: Delays primary survey in a trauma patient
nurse_response: Doctor, while we talked, his breathing has picked up and he's paler.

options.text: Send him for a routine, non-urgent X-ray before anything else.
options.protocol_alignment: Removes an unstable trauma patient from direct observation for a non-urgent step
nurse_response: Doctor, he deteriorated in the corridor on the way to X-ray -- we need to act immediately.

RECOVERING: The scan confirmed intra-abdominal bleeding, Doctor. What's the plan?
DETERIORATING: Doctor, he's still declining -- what now?
CRITICAL: Doctor, he's critical -- we need definitive action.

options.text: Start IV fluid resuscitation, give oxygen, and activate the surgical team for urgent laparotomy assessment.
options.protocol_alignment: Correct escalation for suspected solid-organ injury with hemodynamic compromise
nurse_response: He's responding to fluids, Doctor. Surgical team is on the way.

options.text: Give him something for the pain and continue watching.
options.protocol_alignment: Fails to address the underlying hemorrhage
nurse_response: Doctor, pain relief isn't going to fix internal bleeding -- he's getting worse.

options.text: Wait for the surgical team to arrive before doing anything further.
options.protocol_alignment: Delays resuscitation that should start immediately, in parallel with the surgical call
nurse_response: Doctor, we shouldn't wait -- let's start resuscitating him now while surgery is on the way.

options.text: Discharge him to the ward for observation, since he's still talking.
options.protocol_alignment: Unsafe disposition for a patient with suspected active internal hemorrhage
nurse_response: Doctor! He's arrested on the ward -- bringing him back to resus now!

recoverability_rule.explanation: Resolves outcome_if_prior_state_recoverable vs outcome_if_prior_state_unrecoverable, matching the same rule used in Level 1 and Level 2: reaching full ARREST before the final decision is the only unrecoverable prior state -- even the optimal D3 option cannot guarantee saving him from there. UNSTABLE_RECOVERING, CRITICAL and PERI_ARREST are all still recoverable via the optimal option. Farhan reaches ARREST only if the player chooses the worst option at every prior decision (D1_FARHAN:B/C/D -> D2_FARHAN:B/C/D -> D2_FARHAN option D specifically triggers ARREST). This is the level's genuine death path: repeated bad decisions compound into a state no final decision can undo.

UNSTABLE_RECOVERING: He's improving, Doctor, but still needs close monitoring before we move to Lakshmi.
CRITICAL: Doctor, this may be our last chance with him.
PERI_ARREST: Doctor, he's peri-arrest -- we need definitive action now.
ARREST: Doctor, he has arrested -- we're starting resuscitation now.

options.text: Confirm he's stable enough for surgical handover, hand over clearly, then move to reassess Lakshmi.
options.protocol_alignment: Completes the reassess-and-stabilize loop before shifting attention
nurse_response_success: Farhan is stable for theatre, Doctor.
nurse_response_failure: Doctor, despite resuscitation, we were unable to bring Farhan back.

options.text: Leave him with no clear handover and move on.
options.protocol_alignment: Incomplete handover of an unstable trauma patient
nurse_response_partial: He's holding for now, Doctor, but the surgical team wasn't given a clear picture.
nurse_response_failure: Doctor, despite resuscitation, we were unable to bring Farhan back.

options.text: Continue managing him well past the point he's stable, delaying attention to anyone else waiting.
options.protocol_alignment: Fails to reprioritize once the first patient is stabilized; wastes time that another waiting patient needs
nurse_response_partial: Doctor, Farhan is fine, but we've lost time we didn't need to lose.
nurse_response_failure: Doctor, despite resuscitation, we were unable to bring Farhan back.

options.text: Discontinue monitoring once he looks a bit better, without confirming stability.
options.protocol_alignment: Premature de-escalation of monitoring in an unstable trauma patient
nurse_response_partial: Doctor, he dipped again after we stopped monitoring -- we caught it just in time.
nurse_response_failure: Doctor, despite resuscitation, we were unable to bring Farhan back.

nurse_dialogue: Lakshmi's been waiting, Doctor. Her arm is still deformed and she's in a lot of pain, but her vitals have stayed normal the whole time.
What would you like to do?

options.text: Reassess neurovascular status of the limb, give appropriate analgesia, splint the arm, and send for an X-ray.
options.protocol_alignment: ESI-4-consistent management: analgesia and imaging without over-using critical resources
nurse_response: She's much more comfortable, Doctor. X-ray shows a simple closed fracture -- no neurovascular compromise.

options.text: Tell her to keep waiting since Farhan's case was more urgent and she is stable.
options.protocol_alignment: Fails to manage a patient's ongoing pain once resources are available -- pain control is part of appropriate ESI-4 care
nurse_response: Doctor, she's in a lot of distress now -- we can manage her pain even though she's not the top priority.

options.text: Order a full trauma CT series for her, even though her injury is an isolated limb deformity.
options.protocol_alignment: Over-ordering for an isolated stable injury; resource waste
nurse_response: Doctor, the CT was unnecessary for an isolated arm injury, and it delayed her pain relief.

options.text: Splint the arm immediately without checking distal pulses or sensation first.
options.protocol_alignment: Skips neurovascular assessment before immobilizing a deformed limb
nurse_response: Doctor, we splinted it, but we should check her fingers for circulation and feeling before we finish.

nurse_dialogue: Her X-ray confirms a simple closed radius fracture, Doctor. What's the final plan for her?

options.text: Confirm neurovascular status is intact, arrange orthopedic follow-up, and discharge with clear safety-netting advice.
options.protocol_alignment: Appropriate ESI-4 disposition
nurse_response_success: She's comfortable and safe for discharge, Doctor, with an orthopedic follow-up booked.

options.text: Discharge her immediately without checking circulation/sensation or arranging follow-up.
options.protocol_alignment: Skips essential final checks before discharge
nurse_response_partial: Doctor, she called back later -- her fingers had gone numb. We should have checked before discharge.

options.text: Keep her admitted for observation despite a simple, stable closed fracture.
options.protocol_alignment: Unnecessary resource use (an inpatient bed) for a condition that does not require admission
nurse_response_success: She's fine, Doctor, but admitting her used a bed that a sicker patient may have needed.

options.text: Leave her splinted arm unaddressed and move on without finalizing a plan.
options.protocol_alignment: No disposition plan
nurse_response_partial: Doctor, she's still sitting here waiting to know what happens next.

flow_control.explanation: next_decision inside a decision option NEVER points to a different patient's chain -- it only ever points to another node within the SAME patient's decision_tree chain, or is null when that patient's chain has ended (chain_status: '<PATIENT>_CHAIN_COMPLETE' / a node flagged chain_terminal_node: true). Movement between patients is controlled ONLY by the sequence below, driven by the game engine, never by an option's own next_decision.

sequence.on_complete: advance to step 2 (engine reads the chosen patient order from D0_TRIAGE's effect, but gameplay always resolves P1's full chain before P2's)

endings.combined_outcome_logic: Level 3 is complete once both FARHAN_* and LAKSHMI_* outcomes are reached. Overall level result = SUCCESS only if both patients reach a STABILIZED or PARTIAL_STABILIZATION outcome; overall level result = FAILURE if either patient reaches a CRITICAL_ENDPOINT.

performance_report_schema.triage_accuracy: boolean - whether D0_TRIAGE option A (correct ESI-based prioritization) was selected
